New investment in an AI-powered B2B partnerships business
Mindflair plc, the AIM-quoted company focused on investing in Artificial Intelligence ("AI") related technology, is pleased to note that Sure Valley Ventures' second fund ("SVV2"), in which Mindflair holds an interest, has led a
$1.6 million pre-seed inves
tment round into
Joi
n
Souk
L
td
(
"So
uk"
)
, a British technology business developing an AI Partner Manager for
busi
ness
-to
-bu
siness
(
B2B
)
companies.
The round also includes participation from Antler, Fuel Ventures and strategic angel investors from across the B2B software industry. The funding will be deployed into product development as Souk builds out the core architecture of its AI platform.
Souk h
as developed an AI Partner Manager designed to help companies reactivate dormant partner relationships and improve the performance of B2B partnership programmes. Its autonomous AI agent, Coco, is intended to manage the partnership lifecycle, including sour
cing partners, maintaining engagement, tracking performance and managing payouts.
Souk is addressing a market in which many partner programmes remain heavily reliant on manual processes, spreadsheets and email. According to information provided by Souk, i
ts early deployments have sourced partnerships expected to contribute seven figures in pipeline, secured contracts with several unicorn companies and reduced the manual work required for partner acquisition.
Souk was founded in July 2025 by Leo Crowe, Sofia Hamilton and Ayo
Alfonso
, whose backgrounds include experience at Deel, BlackRock and GitHub. The business is based in London and is focused on building an AI-native platform for partnership management.
Nicholas Lee, Director of Mindflair plc, commented:
"
Souk is applying AI to an important but often under-managed area of B2B growth. Its platform is designed to automate the labour-intensive work involved in managing partner relationships and help companie
s derive greater value from existing networks. We are pleased to see SVV lead this funding round, which will support Souk as it continues to develop its product and build the business."
The Directors of the Company are responsible for the release of this announcement. The person who arranged for the release of this information is Nicholas Lee, a director of the Company.

company_30s.what_they_do: MFAI is a UK‑based AI platform that builds software solutions for other businesses.  Their main product is a low‑code, data‑driven AI engine that lets companies automate decision‑making and analytics without needing a full data science team.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The market for AI‑powered B2B tools is expanding fast, especially in government and regulated sectors where data compliance is critical.  MFAI’s focus on easy integration and compliance gives it a competitive edge against larger, more complex vendors.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in a growth‑phase, raising capital and forming strategic partnerships.  It hasn’t yet turned a profit and is likely burning cash while scaling its platform and customer base.  The share price sits well below what peers charge for similar tech, leaving a large valuation gap for a potential rebound.

rns_narrative: MFAI has been busy securing new AI‑B2B partnership deals and hosting an investor webinar, signalling a push to broaden its customer reach and raise fresh capital.
The company is also being spotlighted in several government‑tech forums, hinting at potential public‑sector contracts that could provide steady revenue streams.
Recent announcements show a mix of funding activity, strategic alliances, and a focus on compliance‑ready solutions—key signs that the firm is positioning itself for a stable, long‑term growth path.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quietly hopeful – the community is listening but not yet convinced.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders highlight MFAI’s AI‑B2B focus and government‑tech exposure as a recipe for future upside, especially if a big partnership lands.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Many skeptics point to the lack of revenue and high cash burn, warning that the company could struggle to survive without a clear path to profitability.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has stayed flat; no new chatter has emerged, which actually strengthens the contrarian case.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for MFAI is flat, giving the setup the maximum surprise potential when a catalyst hits.

near_term_catalysts: The investor webinar scheduled for the end of September could announce a new funding round or a flagship partnership.
A formal partnership announcement with a government agency or a major private sector client would validate the business model.
If the company releases a mid‑year earnings report showing a reduction in burn or a new revenue stream, that would be a strong bounce trigger.
A spike in trading volume that breaks out of the 52‑week low zone would signal capitulation is over.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 3‑day volume surge above the 20‑day moving average, a price break above the recent support cluster, and any news of a new client or funding commitment.
expect_next.timing_regime: MFAI is deep in a crash phase – the price has fallen far below its historical lows and there is no active trading chatter.  The APEX score indicates a tight range, suggesting the next move could be a sharp rebound once a catalyst confirms that the market is ready to re‑value the platform.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock is trading at a level that is more than 70% below its all‑time high, a classic deep‑crash scenario.  If the price recovers to the midpoint of its 52‑week range, the upside is roughly 200% – far higher than the limited downside.  The APEX score shows a tight compression, which often precedes a breakout.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company has no current revenue and is heavily reliant on external funding.  A failure to secure new capital or a major partnership could push the share into a delisting zone.  The worst case is a 30‑day flat or a 20% further decline if the market remains indifferent.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Risk is capped at the small amount of capital you allocate – a 5% loss on a $10,000 position is $500.  Reward potential is a 200% gain, or $20,000, giving a 1:4 risk‑to‑reward ratio.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback to the 20‑day moving average, size 1–2% of your portfolio, and set a stop 10% below that support level.  Use a trailing stop to lock in gains once the price climbs.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until the investor webinar or a partnership announcement occurs.  If the price breaks the 52‑week low and volume rises by 30% over the last 5 days, consider a quick entry.
playbook.if_passing: Only exit if a bankruptcy filing, a regulatory sanction, or a forced delisting notice is issued.

ai_insights.bottom_line: MFAI’s deep crash, coupled with an upcoming partnership announcement and no market chatter, makes it a high‑reward contrarian play with a well‑defined downside.
